sum: A two-week circuit up the Budhi Gandaki gorge to the Tibetan-influenced villages of Nubri and over the Larkya La to the Annapurna side, with rest days at Sama Gaun and Samdo.

guide.note: Manaslu is a restricted area: the permit comes only through a registered agency and a licensed guide must walk with you. Since 22 March 2026 the Department of Immigration issues it to a single trekker as well, so you no longer need a partner to apply. On this route the guide earns the fee on the pass day, setting the pace in the dark, judging snow and weather and knowing when to turn back.

access: Drive from Kathmandu to Machha Khola in a long day, by local bus or private jeep through Dhading Besi and Arughat. The trek ends on the Annapurna Circuit road at Dharapani, where jeeps run down to Besisahar for a bus or car back to Kathmandu or Pokhara.

photo.a: A whitewashed gateway chorten hung with prayer flags stands on the trail among pines, with the twin snow summits of Manaslu rising behind under a clear blue sky.
photo.c: Gateway chorten on the trail to Sama Gaun, below Manaslu

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Manaslu restricted-area permit, MCAP and ACAP
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
bus or shared jeep to the trailhead and back from Besisahar

permits.name: Manaslu restricted area permit
permits.fee: USD 100 per person for the first 7 days, then USD 15 a day

fees.per: person for the first 7 days, then USD 15 a day
person for the first 7 days, then USD 10 a day

permits.where: Department of Immigration in Kathmandu (the Pokhara immigration office also issues them), through a registered trekking agency only.

permits.name: Manaslu Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site or at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu. In practice your agency arranges it with the restricted-area permit.

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

transportText: Bus or a jeep seat from Kathmandu to the start of the trail; at the end a jeep seat down to Besisahar and a bus to Kathmandu
tips: Bring all your cash from Kathmandu; there are no cash machines on the route until Besisahar.
Keep both rest days. If you are short of time, save it on the road days at either end, not at Sama Gaun or Samdo.
Carry microspikes and a headtorch with spare batteries for the pass, and gaiters if there is snow.
Charging, Wi-Fi and hot water cost extra and get scarce above Samdo; carry a power bank.
Treat all water. Above Sama Gaun, fill bottles the night before, because taps and streams freeze by morning.

days.t: Drive from Kathmandu to Machha Khola
days.note: A full day on the road: highway to the Dhading turn-off, then slower and rougher through Arughat and Soti Khola, with the last hours on a narrow dirt track above the river. After heavy rain vehicles may stop short and you walk the rest.

A long day in the gorge, up and down over spurs, across gravel bars and along walkways fixed to the cliff. The hot spring at Tatopani is a good place to cool your feet. This stretch was badly damaged by the October 2026 flood; expect signed diversions and rough temporary trail.

Permits are checked as you leave Jagat. Climb to the large Gurung village of Philim, pass the turning for Tsum where the Siyar Khola joins from the right, then enter a narrow gorge of bamboo and pine, crossing the river several times before the short climb to Deng.

The valley turns west and the villages become Tibetan in character, with carved mani walls at Bihi and Ghap. After Ghap the trail climbs for about two hours through tall forest of fir, oak and rhododendron, loud with the river, to the checkpost and lodges at Namrung.

A short day on purpose now that you are passing 3,000 m. The trail climbs through the barley terraces of Lihi and Sho to Lho, with Himalchuli and then Manaslu coming into view. Walk up to Ribung Gompa in the afternoon for the view.

An easy morning through pine and rhododendron forest to the open terrace of Shyala, ringed by peaks, then across the stream from the Pungyen glacier to the fields and long main street of Sama Gaun. Arrive by lunch and rest.

Walk up to Pungyen Gompa, on a yak pasture under Manaslu's east face, and come back down for the night. The short alternative is Birendra Tal, under an hour from the village. The long one is Manaslu Base Camp, a hard seven to eight hours that suits only people already going strongly.

A gentle walk up the wide valley past long mani walls, with juniper and birch giving way to open yak pasture. A wooden bridge and a short climb bring you to Samdo by midday. Keep the pace slow; the afternoon is for rest.

Climb the hillside behind the village as far as feels comfortable; most people turn round somewhere between 4,300 and 4,600 m, with a view back to Manaslu. The full-day walk towards the Tibet border is an option only if you are going well.

Cross the Budhi Gandaki, here little more than a stream, and climb steadily above the moraine of the Larkya glacier to the huts and tents of Dharamsala. It is a short day on purpose. Eat early, lay out your warm layers and headtorch, and try to sleep.

days.t: Over the Larkya La to Bhimtang
days.note: Leave between 3 and 4 am. Four to five hours of gradual climbing over moraine and past frozen ponds lead to the prayer flags at the top. The descent is steep, loose and often icy for the first hour, then eases along the moraine to Bhimtang. There is almost no shelter and no reliable water on the way.

Cross the moraine and the stream below Bhimtang, then descend through tall forest of rhododendron, pine and oak to Gho and the stone village of Tilije. A jeep track covers the last hour and a half to the Annapurna checkpoint at Dharapani. It is 1,860 m of descent in a day; if your knees complain, stop at Tilije.

days.t: Jeep to Besisahar and drive to Kathmandu
days.note: Shared jeeps take three to four rough hours down the Marsyangdi gorge to Besisahar, where you change to a bus, microbus or car for the six to seven hours to Kathmandu. It is a long day, and traffic on the highway makes the time unpredictable; many people break it with a night in Besisahar.
